blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust in the Public Sector & Government context — regulation-first design, a fixed delivery rhythm, and outcomes your board can audit.

In Public Sector & Government, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Aging systems with hardening debt meet rising state-grade threats; accreditation cycles slow every change.
Benefits, tax, health and licensing systems never joined; citizens re-submit the same facts to every agency. Fraud and error hide in the seams.
Permits, claims and case files are paper-shaped; processing times measured in months erode trust and increase cost per case.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

7 services from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower make up the delivery pattern — Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management as the usual core — run through the Dataq Method with Accessibility (Section 508 / EN 301 549 / WCAG) obligations baked into the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.
Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Identity-centric access across agencies and third parties (state-grade threat surface reduced with evidence)
CBOM and migration for decade-retention data (harvest exposure closed early)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: Accessibility (Section 508 / EN 301 549 / WCAG) and Accessibility (Section 508 / EN 301 549 / WCAG). Digital services must meet accessibility mandates. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

A fixed rhythm keeps progress visible from week one — here is the one we run. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
